conbody.p: Once you have a recording, Audacity offers several core editing techniques. This topic collects four of them; each is large enough to deserve its own topic.

section.title: Trimming
section.p: Trimming removes unwanted audio from the start, end, or middle of a clip. Select a region in the waveform and press Delete to remove it; the surrounding audio closes the gap. Use trimming to cut silence, false starts, and mistakes before you process the track.

section.title: Fading
section.p: Fades smooth the start and end of a clip so audio eases in and out instead of clicking on. Select the region to fade, then choose EffectFade In or Fade Out. Fades are essential for clean transitions between segments.

section.title: Normalizing
section.p: Normalization raises (or lowers) the level of a clip so its loudest peak sits at a target level, giving consistent loudness across clips. Choose EffectNormalize and set the peak amplitude, typically around -1 dB.

section.title: Removing Noise
section.p: Noise reduction removes steady background noise such as hum or hiss. Capture a noise profile from a quiet section, then apply the Noise Reduction effect to the whole track. Apply it before normalization and compression so you shape clean audio.
